# SUMS

SUMS is a free daily number puzzle game at https://sums.games, created by Xavier Games. You fill a grid by counting up. 1, 2 and 3 start on the board. To place the next number, tap a chain of numbers that adds up to it, each touching the one before (diagonals count), then tap an empty square touching the last number in the chain. Fill every square that isn't a wall to win.

There are two puzzles each day:
- Mini SUMS: 5×5 grid for a short solve.
- Full SUMS: 7×7 grid with more planning, clues, and walls.

New Mini and Full puzzles publish every day at midnight Eastern Time (America/New_York). The game is free, ad-supported, and does not require an account. Personal statistics, streaks, and best times are stored in the browser.

Hard mode limits how many cells you can select at once, typically three or four. There is no time limit.

Weekly difficulty ramps from Monday (difficulty 1) to Sunday (difficulty 7).

## How to play

1. Read the starting grid. Gray numbers come with the puzzle, including 1, 2 and 3. Black squares are walls. Every other empty square gets a number from you.
2. Count up in order. Your first number is 4, then 5, then 6. Numbers go in order and you can't skip ahead.
3. Tap a chain that adds up to the next number. Each number in the chain must touch the one before it, and diagonals count. Your first move is usually 1 + 3 = 4.
4. Place it next to the end of your chain. Tap an empty square touching the last number in your chain. The new number appears there.
5. Earn the gray numbers. When the count reaches a gray number, a chain of numbers touching it has to add up to it, and then the count moves on. Plan ahead so that chain will exist, and undo if it can't.
6. Fill every square. The puzzle is solved when every square that isn't a wall has a number. Undo and Hint are always there if you get stuck.

## FAQ

### What is SUMS?
SUMS is a free daily number puzzle at sums.games. You fill a grid by counting up: to place the next number, tap a chain of touching numbers that adds up to it, then tap an empty square next to the last one. Diagonals count.

### How do you play SUMS?
1, 2 and 3 start on the board, so your first number is 4. Tap a chain of numbers that adds up to the next number, each touching the one before it (diagonals count), then tap an empty square touching the last number in the chain. Gray numbers come with the puzzle, but when you reach one, a chain touching it has to add up to it. Fill every square that isn't a wall to win.

### Do diagonals count in SUMS?
Yes. Every square touches the eight squares around it, including diagonals. That applies both to building a chain and to placing the number.

### Why won't SUMS let me place a number?
The square has to be empty and touch the last number in your chain, and the chain has to add up to exactly the next number. If all of that is true and it's still refused, putting the number there would leave the next gray number with no chain touching it that adds up to it.

### Is SUMS free to play?
Yes. You do not need an account, app download, or subscription.

### What is the difference between Mini SUMS and Full SUMS?
Mini is 5×5 and usually takes a few minutes. Full is 7×7 and needs more planning. Both refresh daily.

### When does the daily SUMS puzzle reset?
Midnight Eastern Time.

### Do I need an account to play SUMS?
No. Open https://sums.games and play immediately.

### What is Hard mode in SUMS?
Hard mode limits how many cells you can select at once, typically to three or four.

### Is there a time limit?
No. Completion time is tracked for personal stats and optional high scores.

### Who created SUMS?
Xavier Games. Contact: harrison.x.becker@gmail.com.
